facts.text: The AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles were heated in situ from 298 K to 973 K at a rate of 1 K/s.
The heated nanoparticles were analyzed using aberration-corrected STEM and atomistic molecular-dynamics simulations.
In situ heating was performed under vacuum.
Measurements were conducted at heating steps of 473, 673, 773, 873, and 973 K.
Analysis at each temperature step was limited to 45 minutes to mitigate infrared-radiation effects on EDS.
Surface-energy differences drove Au and Cu atoms to segregate to the nanoparticle surface.
Atomic diffusion became active rather than remaining sluggish, showing that the evolving structure was kinetically controlled rather than stabilized by configurational entropy.
Particle reshaping and coalescence enhanced local atomic diffusion and surface segregation.
The surface-segregated Au and Cu formed a shell that melted and evaporated at 973 K.
Thermal stability deteriorated above approximately 673 K, with progressive disappearance of the smallest 2–4 nm nanoparticles and widening of the particle-size distribution.
Increasing temperature changed the nanoparticles from elliptical toward spherical shapes.
Au/Cu evaporation produced a reported 22% reduction in nanoparticle size.
